items.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He says, “Josh is taking piano lessons now.”

ctx.x: “Why don’t you do it again and say it” – now I’m going to add – do it the way you – so I did it, and they sent it back to him. He said, “Perfect.” Then he said, “We’re going to record in Montreal.” I had already done something up in – I can’t ever think of the name of that town – Palmdale, somewhere up there. They’d shot something up there. Catherine Zeta-Jones was in it. But they were going to do my part in Montreal. The reason they wanted to do it – the picture was called The Terminal – they had rented an…

“Tom, where’d you get that suit? I got to get one just like it” – so he comes up to me, and he’s speaking with this accent. After the scene, I said, “You sound just like Dracula.” He wanted my autograph. He was reticent to talk to me. The band started to vamp Killer Joe. I said, “I got to play now, but when I finish, I’ll give you the autograph.” That was the last scene. Then when I gave him the autograph – Steven had gotten me to sign my autograph on a piece of paper, and he used that. I was supposed to sign…

Steven is a down-to-earth guy. He looks you right in the eye. None of that stuff. And Tom. Humble. If you didn’t know who they were, you’d just think it was another guy. Incredible. I love him, and what he does. Tom Hanks has come a long ways. And Thelma Hopkins, who used to be in Bosom Buddies, where he got his start – Thelma Hopkins and him. The two guys played – masqueraded as women.
